newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures close mixed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures close mixed in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed mixed in thin trade, but a late afternoon rally in Standard & Poor's 500s gave the market a positive tone ahead of Tuesday's U.S. elections, traders and analysts said.
Late in the day, December S&Ps shot up to 711.50 on buy-stop orders. Dealer buying also escalated in the afternoon, as one major U.S. firm bought a total of 1,000 contracts all day.
"Really, today was a non-event," one floor trader said, adding that estimated volume in the December contract did not even total 60,000 contracts.
The U.S. bond market also traded higher, but in tentative, light trade ahead of the U.S. Treasury's auction of three- and 10-year notes and 30-year T-bonds this week.

Traders in every U.S. market also noted some concern about the outcome of Tuesday's U.S. elections. Analysts and traders will be closely watching Congressional races to see whether the Republicans retain control of the House of Representatives and the Senate.
A Democratic upset in Congress could weaken U.S. markets across the board and drag the U.S. dollar lower, they said.
Nikkei futures finished slightly lower. December Nikkeis had turned unchanged during the day, erasing slim losses after the dollar/yen's rally to the 114.00 spot level.

Fair value for December S&Ps was at 2.97 points to cash. Several arbitrage buy programs were noted throughout the day when the contract's premium against cash widened more than 4.00 points, traders said.

At the end of pit trade, December S&Ps rose 4.75 points to 711.25, KBT Value Lines were up 1.95 at 648.10, New Composites were up 2.30 at 377.25, Nikkeis retreated slightly to end down 15.0 at 20,655, Midcap 400s were up 0.75 at 244.95 and Nasdaq 100s were up 0.40 at 763.00. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
